public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI labs' 'AI safety' talk, including Amodei's, never addresses actual harms of the products they build today.

statement.excerpt: Dario Amodei of Anthropic took to CBS to say that for “too long” the industry had “lied” about risks, saying that the “biggest one” was killing all humans, never mentioning when an LLM convinced a teenager to kill himself or its own hacking incidents because “AI safety” never relates to the things they’re building today.
statement.document_title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

from_speaker: to the things they’re building today
our_interpretation: Assess the supplied normalized proposition: labs' public safety communications never address actual harms involving their existing products.
Addressing includes discussing observed misuse, harmful interactions, and safeguards for deployed products. It does not require acknowledging legal responsibility or proving safeguards effective.
The word never extends the claim to public communications before the post. No artificial starting date or reporting quarter is imposed.
The narrower claim about omissions in the CBS interview is not treated as equivalent to the broader claim about all safety discourse.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive record shows safety communications confined to hypothetical future harms, with no discussion of harms involving existing products.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one public, pre-post safety communication directly discusses harms or misuse involving an existing product.
